summary: Red team of the extraction of André, 'La conjecture du facteur direct' (Publ. Math. IHÉS 127, 2018), against the published PDF, whose hash matches. There are six findings: one high, three medium and two low. The 191 items are faithful to the published text. All 23 library claims hold at the pins, and all 25 source-issue verdicts check out. What breaks is ownership. (1) Three source routes point to blueprints finished before the paper was accepted: PerfectoidSpaces P0–P7 and AdicSpacesPartII. Neither plans the appendix A.4 almost purity used in §3.3, the §1.2 Weierstrass-localisation unit-ball package used in Theorem 2.5.2, or the perfectoidness of the coordinate tower, so fourteen items are planned nowhere. Route 6 also cites the companion's R0 ownership, which REV-PAPER-ANDRE-18 rejected. (2) Beyond the confirmed RT-AREA-padic-1/2, three further companion imports have no owner: Corollaire 2.9.3 (the whole of Lemma 2.5.1), Exemples 3.2.3 and Lemma 4.2.3 (used for Theorem 4.4.2). (3) Balanced big CM predicates and splinters are planned twice, here and in the accepted BHATT-ETAL-23 Scheme-foundations Part II. (4) The equal-characteristic existence of big CM algebras, which Theorem 0.7.1 and §4.3 use (also via a characteristic-p minimal-prime quotient), has no item. Low: step (a) of 2.5.2 is asserted without an argument, and a complete-module flatness criterion (Stacks 15.28.4) makes it and Berkovich 2.2.4 unnecessary; Corollary 2.6.1 is narrowed to finite indices.

Source. Published PDF, Publ. Math. IHÉS 127 (2018) 71–93, from https://www.numdam.org/item/10.1007/s10240-017-0097-9.pdf, fetched 2026-09-30. It has 23 pages and SHA-256 34da107d0b96149d9a6779ec1694a0cbb096136d021114b59427024ef3d47053, which matches the extraction. I read the whole paper in a pdftotext extraction. I rendered pp.82, 86 and 92 at 300 dpi to settle symbols: 𝔨 in Corollary 2.6.1, the ≠ and ⊄ in Lemma 4.1.3 (a)/(b), '(π) ∩ A = pgA ⊄ p²A' in §4.2, and the A.4 intermediate-module sentence behind E10.
Versions and errata. arXiv 1609.00345 has only v1. Crossref has no update or correction relation for 10.1007/s10240-017-0097-9 (queried 2026-09-30). No erratum was found.

Items. All 191 statements and locators were checked against the published text: §§0.1–0.8, 1.1–1.2, 2.1–2.6.1, 3.1–3.4, 4.1–4.4, A.1–A.4 and the bibliography. Locators use the published pagination. The mathematics was re-verified for: 0.1.1/0.2.1 (direct-summand, unramified-direct-summand); 0.7.1/0.7.2 with the E20 repair (a counterexample check with R = k[[x,y]], S = R × R/(x)); 4.4.2 and hh-cm-descent (the purity argument); 4.1.3 (a)/(b); 3.3 (Lemma 1.1.2 with R ∩ 𝔨 ∋ pg, which needs m ≥ 2); 2.6.1; Lemma 1.1.1–1.1.2; flat-annihilator; fp-ideal-descent; colimit-base-flatness (faithfulness via 1 ∉ m_j M); discriminant-element; reduction-to-domain; galois-closure-reduction; cohen-parameter-presentation; no-unramified-square, including why (2) implies (3); discriminant-pullback-obstruction; §1.2 formulas (1)–(6); weierstrass-nonzerodivisor; perfect-closure-trace-retraction. On the last: in a perfect ring radical ideals are perfect, so 'radical, hence not in (T)' is valid.

Source issues. I verified all 25 against the page. E1, E2, E3, E6, E10 (page image), E15, E16 and E25 (with g = 1 the union is W(k)[ζ_{p^∞}][[T]]^, which has no T^{1/p}) hold as misprints or errors. Missed issues: one gap (finding 5). Candidates checked and not reported: '(π) ∩ A = pgA' on p.86 (only '∌ p²A' is used); 𝔨 in Corollary 2.6.1 (typeset correctly).

findings.claim: Three source routes send material to layers whose blueprints were finished and accepted without it, so fourteen items that lie on the proof of the main theorems are now planned nowhere, and one planned item is planned only in a narrower generality. (a) Route 2: André's appendix A.4 (almost-pure module maps, testing through the left adjoint, Lemma A.4.1 on almost lifting and almost-zero Ext classes, almost-pure algebra maps through ( )_!!, left factors) is used in Corollary 3.2.2 and §3.3, the step that kills the splitting obstruction modulo p^m. The PerfectoidSpaces P0–P7 blueprint was accepted with P0 'source_decomposed' and has no such node. (b) Route 6: the §1.2 package (the Weierstrass localisation B{f/λ} = B⟨U⟩/(λU − f), formulas (1)–(6), the λU − f non-zero-divisor lemma, the ϖ-adic topology of B≤1, and invariance §1.2.3) is the analytic input of Theorem 2.5.2 (formulas (13), (14), (17)). The accepted AdicSpacesPartII blueprint has none of it. The route also rests on a false premise: its reason says 'Reuse the companion PAPER-ANDRE-18 ownership of generic uniform-Banach norm/completion comparisons … at R0'. But REV-PAPER-ANDRE-18 rejected exactly that route, 89 minutes after this paper's review: 'R0's admissible geometric morphism/tensor-product contract does not own a generic norm-comparison package merely by importing topological algebra'. The R0 stage text, and RS-05's narrowed keeps for R0, mention neither Weierstrass localisations of normed algebras nor unit balls. Only uniform-banach-algebra itself is covered, by nodes of that packet. (c) Route 3: coordinate-tower-perfectoid (Â_∞0 = the completion of ∪_j W(k)[ζ_(p^j)][[T^(1/p^j)]], and Â_∞0⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩, are perfectoid K̂_∞-algebras) has no node. cyclotomic-perfectoid-field is marked planned at P1 for K_0 = Frac W(k) with k any perfect field; André needs arbitrary perfect k, and §4.2 passes to W(k^(1/p^∞)). The P1 node covers only ℚ_p^cycl, and its P3 companion only finite extensions of ℚ_p.

findings.claim: Several companion results that this paper's items import are owned by nothing. The fix already written for RT-AREA-padic-1/2 would not change that. That confirmed finding handles André's perfectoid Abhyankar lemma, via Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 10.9 with J = (g). Its fix (RT-AREA-padic-1.fixes.md, /2, edit 3) records only PAPER-ANDRE-18/2.9.3-root-algebras, /3.6.1-root-algebra-perfectoid and /2.9.2-tubular-colimit as gaps. It does not name three imports that this paper actually uses. (a) PAPER-ANDRE-18/2.9.3-root-as-colimit, companion Corollaire 2.9.3 (2.32): ucolim_i A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩{(T−g)/ϖ^i}^u ≅ A⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩, with unit balls. It is the whole content of Lemma 2.5.1 ('c'est un cas particulier de [1, cor. 2.9.3]', p.79), on which Theorem 2.5.2 rests. (b) PAPER-ANDRE-18/3.2.3-standard-examples: A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid for perfectoid A, with its universal property. p.79 cites '[1, ex. 3.2.3 (1)]'. (c) PAPER-ANDRE-18/4.2.2-integral-closure: g^(−1/p^∞)A° is the complete integral closure of A° in A[1/g]. This is companion Lemma 4.2.3, cited on p.88 ('intégralement fermé dans D′[1/(pg)] car D′[1/p] est perfectoïde sur K̂_∞, cf. [1, 4.2.3]') to build δ: D → D′ for Theorem 4.4.2. All three are 'missing' in PAPER-ANDRE-18 and routed only by its rejected route 2. So the pending design DESIGN-PerfectoidSpacesPartII, which follows route 4's brief, would import them from nowhere.

findings.claim: The (balanced) big Cohen–Macaulay predicates are planned by two accepted routes with no link between them. Route 1 of this paper plans them for algebras (Definition 4.1.1(1)–(2)) in the new commutative-algebra roadmap. PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23 route 10, accepted five minutes after this paper's review, plans them for arbitrary modules in the Scheme-foundations Part II. Its brief says 'Build big/balanced/cohomological CM predicates'. The splinter notion there (every finite injective extension splits) is exactly what direct-summand proves for regular rings. Neither extraction, review nor brief mentions the other. The two pending designs will therefore define the same predicate twice, and the module form is the more general one.
findings.evidence: PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23.result.json: /big-cm '§2.2(b)': 'M is big CM when some system of parameters is weakly regular on M and M/mM≠0; no finite-generation hypothesis on M'. /balanced-cm '§2.2(c)': 'Every system of parameters of the local Noetherian base is weakly regular on M, and M/mM≠0'. /splinter 'Definition2.12': 'every finite injective ring map out of it admits an R-linear retraction'. All are missing, in route 10, whose review verdict is 'accept' (commit f7737bf9, 2026-09-23 19:09). Its brief: 'Build big/balanced/cohomological CM predicates, closure vanishing, B⁰ …'. Issue #3361 (DESIGN-SchemeAndStackFoundationsPartII) lists that route with 195 items. PAPER-ANDRE-18-B.result.json /big-cm-fixed and /big-cm-balanced are the same predicates for a B-algebra C (Definition 4.1.1, p.84; André's footnote 5: '“big Cohen-Macaulay algebra" ou “balanced big Cohen-Macaulay algebra"'). A grep of both result.json files and both review files finds no cross-reference.

findings.claim: Two things are missing. (a) The existence of balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebras for Noetherian local rings containing a field has no item. Theorem 0.7.1 is stated for every Noetherian local ring B, and André proves only the mixed-characteristic case: 'Le cas où B contient un corps étant déjà connu' (p.75). §4.3 invokes the equal-characteristic case for the components S_{m,i}: 'D'après le th. 0.7.1 (et [17] en égale caractéristique)' (p.87). The extraction's own reduction needs it inside the mixed-characteristic proof too. big-cm-reductions (1) passes to B/P for a minimal prime P with dim B/P = dim B, and B/P can have characteristic p. For example, B = Z_p[[x]]/(px) has minimal primes (p) and (x), with B/(p) = F_p[[x]] and B/(x) = Z_p both of dimension 1. big-cm-existence's note calls the equal-characteristic case 'a prerequisite'. The prerequisites entry for Hochster–Huneke 1995 is marked 'Not read', and no item states the theorem. So route 1 gives it no statement and no owner. (b) direct-summand depends only on unramified-direct-summand and unramified-reduction, but the equal-characteristic splittings are separate inputs. unramified-reduction's first proof step says 'Equal-characteristic cases are separate known inputs'. The items frobenius-direct-summand-char-p and invertible-degree-retraction exist but are not dependencies of direct-summand.
findings.evidence: André, published PDF: p.75, 'Le cas où B contient un corps étant déjà connu, c'est le cas où B est d'inégale caractéristique (0, p) (sans p-torsion) que nous traitons'. p.86, §4.2: 'Après les travaux de Hochster et al., on peut se limiter … au cas où B est d'inégale caractéristique (0,p)'. p.87, §4.3: 'D'après le th. 0.7.1 (et [17] en égale caractéristique), il existe une S_{m,i}-algèbre de Cohen-Macaulay T_{m,i}'. Extraction: big-cm-existence note, 'the equal-characteristic case is Hochster's and is a prerequisite'. big-cm-reductions note, 'reduces the general case to a complete local domain, either containing a field (Hochster, known) or …'. The Hochster–Huneke 1995 prerequisite entry ends 'Not read.'. No item among the 191 states equal-characteristic existence (searched: 'equal', 'contains a field', 'Hochster–Huneke'). direct-summand 'dependencies': ['…/unramified-direct-summand', '…/unramified-reduction'].
findings.fix: Add an item 'big-cm-equal-characteristic': every Noetherian local ring containing a field has a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra. Cite Hochster–Huneke, Infinite integral extensions and Noetherian rings (Ann. of Math. 135, 1992), where R⁺ is big CM for an excellent local domain of characteristic p, and the reduction to characteristic p in characteristic 0 (Hochster–Huneke 1995 / Hochster 1975). Its status is missing, routed to route 1. Add it to the dependencies of big-cm-existence and finite-cover-flat-domination, and to the prerequisites (Hochster–Huneke 1992). Add frobenius-direct-summand-char-p and invertible-degree-retraction to the dependencies of direct-summand, or of unramified-reduction, whose statement covers all Noetherian regular rings.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-ANDRE-18-B.result.json: items generic-fibre-flat, noetherian-stage-faithfully-flat, affinoid-rational-flat; sourceIssues (no entry for proof step (a) of Theorem 2.5.2, p.81)
findings.claim: Step (a) of the proof of Theorem 2.5.2 asserts, without an argument, that A_j0⟨T^{1/p^j}⟩{f_ik/ϖ_ik} is flat over A_j0 = A°_j0[1/p]. A_j0 is not affinoid: it consists of the bounded functions on the open unit polydisc. André gives only that its analytic spectrum is an increasing union of closed polydiscs B_r, over which the Weierstrass localisation is flat (Berkovich 2.2.4). Two steps are left unexplained. One is the passage from flatness over each B_r⟨T^{1/p^j}⟩ to flatness over A_j0. This needs A_j0 → B_r to be flat and the comparison of A_j0⟨T^{1/p^j}⟩{f/ϖ} ⊗_{A_j0} B_r with B_r⟨T^{1/p^j}⟩{f/ϖ}, which is not automatic because the module is not finite over A_j0. The other is the localisation at maximal ideals. The extraction reproduces this as generic-fibre-flat, and makes it depend on affinoid-rational-flat (Berkovich 1990, 'not read'). The step is dispensable. The algebra C = A°_j0⟨T^{1/p^j},U⟩/(ϖ_ik U − f_ik) is ϖ_j-torsion-free: the coefficient computation of §1.2.1 with π = ϖ_j uses only that multiplication by f_ik is isometric, which holds because f_ik has norm 1 in the multiplicatively normed A_j0⟨T^{1/p^j}⟩; the paper relies on the same fact for (17) through formula (2). It is ϖ_j-adically complete, as a quotient of the Noetherian ϖ_j-adically complete ring A°_j0⟨T^{1/p^j},U⟩. Its reduction C/ϖ_j is free over A°_j0/ϖ_j, by step (b). By the local flatness criterion over the nilpotent ideal ϖ_j(A°_j0/ϖ_j^n), each C/ϖ_j^n is flat over A°_j0/ϖ_j^n. The Tor_1 term is {x ∈ C/ϖ_j^n : ϖ_j x = 0}/ϖ_j^{n−1}(C/ϖ_j^n), which is 0 by torsion-freeness. Stacks Lemma 15.28.4 (tag 0912) then gives C = lim C/ϖ_j^n flat over A°_j0. Faithfulness follows as printed. So (a), flatness by fibres and Berkovich 2.2.4 can all be dropped.
findings.evidence: André p.81: '(a) A_j0⟨T^{1/p^j}⟩{f_ik/ϖ_ik} est plate sur A_j0 ; or, le spectre analytique de A_j0 est réunion croissante des polydisques affinoïdes de rayons r ∈ |K°°_∞|, et pour une telle algèbre de Tate B_r, B_r⟨T^{1/p^j}⟩{f_ik/ϖ_ik} est même plate sur B_r⟨T^{1/p^j}⟩ [3, prop. 2.2.4]'. Nothing follows about how flatness over A_j0 is obtained. §1.2.1, p.76: B≤1⟨U⟩/(λU − f) 'est sans π-torsion' when multiplication by f is isometric. §2.4, p.79: 'Les A_j0 sont multiplicativement normées'. Stacks Project Lemma 15.28.4 (tag 0912; read 2026-09-30): 'Let A be a Noetherian ring. Let I be an ideal of A. Let (M_n) be an inverse system of A-modules such that M_n is a flat A/I^n-module, M_{n+1} → M_n is surjective. Then M = lim M_n is a flat A-module'. Extraction: generic-fibre-flat depends on affinoid-rational-flat, whose note says 'Berkovich 1990 was not read (not public)'.

findings.claim: The item narrows Corollary 2.6.1 to finite indices, 'For every finite pair (j,k)', and has no item for the statement the proof actually proves. The paper says 'Pour tout (j, k)', and §2.2 lets either index be ∞ by convention. The proof's content is that A°_∞0 → A°_∞∞ is pure ('Il suffit de montrer que A°_∞∞ est pur sur A°_∞0'). The finite cases follow by composing with the pure map A°_j0 → A°_∞0 and taking a left factor. Infinite-index purity (A°_j0 → A°_j∞, A°_∞0 → A°_∞k, A°_∞0 → A°_∞∞) is therefore stated in the source and missing from the extraction.
findings.evidence: André p.78, §2.2: 'On permet la valeur ∞ pour l'un des indices (ou les deux), en prenant la réunion indexée par les valeurs finies de cet indice'. p.82: 'Corollaire 2.6.1. — Pour tout (j, k), A°_j0 ↪ A°_jk est pur. Démonstration. — Il suffit de montrer que A°_∞∞ est pur sur A°_∞0, puisque ce dernier est pur sur chaque A°_j0' (page image read at 300 dpi).
